_nguon: EN-ALL GĐ 3 — cờ cảnh báo hồ sơ / lá số (chung Tử vi, Bát tự): câu tiếng Anh viết lại từ nghĩa, {slot} giữ nguyên.
co.sinh_nuoc_ngoai: Born abroad: the chart uses the local clock time where you were born, not Vietnam time.
co.gio_mua_he: One hour of daylight saving time has been taken off: local standard time {gio}.
co.gio_doi_mui: Your birth time falls right when clocks changed there (daylight saving starting or ending), so the clock may have been an hour off from the chart shown. If you know the standard time for sure, enter it by hand under "Can't find my city".
co.mui_gio_lam_tron: At that time your birthplace kept a local time with odd minutes; it has been rounded to the nearest time zone to compare against the solar terms.
co.thang_nhuan: Born in the second half of leap month {thang} (day {ngay}): the chart follows the common rule that the second half of a leap month counts as the next month (month {thang_sau}). Some schools count the whole leap month as month {thang} — the Life palace, the Bureau and the stars may then differ.
co.ty_muon_ngay_sau: Born after 23:00: Zi Wei Dou Shu starts the next day at 23:00, so this chart is drawn as if you were born on lunar day {ngay}/{thang} of the {nam} year, in the Rat hour. BaZi and numerology keep day {ngay_goc}/{thang_goc}.
co.ty_muon_ngay_sau_nhuan: Born after 23:00: Zi Wei Dou Shu starts the next day at 23:00, so this chart is drawn as if you were born on lunar day {ngay}/{thang} (leap month) of the {nam} year, in the Rat hour. BaZi and numerology keep day {ngay_goc}/{thang_goc}.
co.lich_viet_trung_trung: Your birth date falls in a stretch where the Vietnamese lunar calendar (UTC+7) and the Chinese one (UTC+8) differ: the chart is shown on the Chinese calendar, as you chose — switching calendars gives a different lunar month or day, so the Life palace, the Bureau and the reading can change.
co.lich_viet_trung_viet: Your birth date falls in a stretch where the Vietnamese lunar calendar (UTC+7) and the Chinese one (UTC+8) differ: the chart is shown on the Vietnamese calendar — switching calendars gives a different lunar month or day, so the Life palace, the Bureau and the reading can change.
co.lich_am_mien_nam: The lunar date follows the calendar used in southern Vietnam in 1960–1975 (UTC+8): it corresponds to {ngay} in the Western calendar.
co.gio_sinh_mat_troi: The chart uses TRUE SOLAR TIME in {noi} (your choice): {gio} ({lech} minutes against standard time {gio_chuan}, from longitude and the equation of time), the {chi} hour. Most books use clock time — switch back in the School settings.
co.gio_mat_troi: By true solar time in {noi} ({gio}) you fall in the {chi_mt} hour rather than the {chi} hour. The chart still uses clock time, as most books do; if it does not fit, look at the other hour's chart too (choose "True solar time" in the School settings).
co.tz_adjusted: Clocks at your birthplace ran on UTC+{utc}; converted to the calendar meridian UTC+7: {gio} on {ngay}.
co.tz_disputed: Your birth date falls in a period where historical sources disagree about the time zone — compare the chart under both assumptions.
co.ty_edge: Your birth time sits close to the Rat-hour boundary (23:00–00:59) — the day pillar is sensitive to a few minutes' error and to which boundary rule is used.
co.tet_edge: You were born {so} day(s) from Lunar New Year (Tet) — the year's stem and branch change right at this boundary. One day off on the birth date changes the whole chart.
co.mui_gio_nuoc_ngoai: The birthplace time zone has not been entered: BaZi is comparing the solar-term changeovers against Vietnam time. If you were born close to a solar-term change (early in a Western calendar month), the month or year pillar may be off — add your birthplace time zone in your profile to get it right.
co.dieu_hau_nam_ban_cau: Climate balance is read from the real season in {noi} (Southern Hemisphere, your choice): when the solar-term month is summer, where you were born it is mid-winter and the other way round — only the element needed for climate (method 1) changes; the four pillars, the structure and method 2 stay the same. This is a modern theory, not found in the classical texts.
co.tiet_edge: Born about {gio} hours from a solar-term change — the month pillar (and possibly the year pillar) switches at this point; a birth time a few dozen minutes off means a different pillar.
co.gio_ty: Born 23:00–23:59: shown under the school that STARTS THE NEXT DAY at 23:00 (your choice) — the day pillar is the next day. The system default keeps that same day's pillar (late Rat hour); the two schools differ only in the day pillar, the hour pillar is the same.
co.da_ty: Born 23:00–23:59 (late Rat hour): this BaZi keeps THAT DAY's day pillar, and takes the hour pillar from the Rat hour of the next day. The school that changes the day at 23:00 gives a different day pillar; Zi Wei Dou Shu on this site moves to the next day.
